title: Lena and the Group Chat
premise: Noor Eastwick just wants to survive senior year unnoticed at Hollow Creek High, a school built over a flooded quarry town. When his lab partner Priya vanishes, leaving only a ring of keys and a phone still buzzing in her locker, Noor discovers she'd been added to a group chat called 'Lena's Keys' — a chat whose members all went missing decades ago. The chat offers him a bargain: win the state swim championship the town obsesses over, and Priya comes back; but the real championship is a memory contest held in the flooded halls below, where he must hold onto every true memory of Priya while the chat slowly trades them away. Noor wins the swim meet to buy time, then dives into the quarry to confront Lena herself, giving up his own best memory — his mother's face — to bring Priya home, ending with Priya safe, Noor remembered by everyone but remembering almost nothing, and one unread message waiting in the chat.
about_author: Coral Galloway is a former swim coach from a river town that was dammed and renamed, and she swears her high school yearbook has one too many faces in it. She writes stories about kids who survive things by refusing to forget.

chapters.title: Head Down, Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Establishes his survival rules at Hollow Creek High — don't talk, don't join, don't remember out loud — and his uneasy friendship with lab partner Priya, who breaks all three rules daily. When she jokes that the school's trophy case has swimmers in it nobody remembers, he laughs it off. Beat: loneliness mistaken for safety.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Priya doesn't show for third period, then not at all. Police find her backpack; in her locker, only a heavy ring of old brass keys and a phone that keeps buzzing. The buzzing is a group chat — 'Lena's Keys' — and the last message, from Priya, reads 'I found the door.' Beat: dread arriving in the shape of an ordinary notification.

chapters.title: Lena's Keys
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, first contact. Replying to the chat, Noor gets answers from six accounts, all with graduation years from the 1970s. They explain the school sits on Old Marlow, drowned when the quarry flooded, and that Priya opened a door with the keys. They offer a trade: win Saturday's swim championship, and the town will 'remember her back.' Beat: the horror of a polite, helpful haunting.

chapters.title: What the Trophy Case Knows
chapters.summary: Noor and skeptical classmate Dez investigate, matching the chat's usernames to faded trophy plaques — six champions, six vanished kids, photos scratched out. The coach catches them but goes pale at the names and tells them to drop it. Beat: the adult world's complicity; the price of survival is silence.

chapters.title: Trials
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. He's a mediocre swimmer with two days to become a champion; the chat 'helps,' and every lap in the pool feels like being watched from below. Meanwhile his own memories start slipping — he can't recall Priya's laugh, only that he used to know it. Beat: the bargain's true cost revealed — memory is the currency.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Race day. Noor swims the race of his life and wins, the gym erupting, the chat congratulating him — then reveals the fine print: the swim title bought him an invitation to the real championship, held tonight, below. Priya isn't returned; she's the prize. Beat: triumph curdling into trap.

chapters.title: Down Where the Streets Have Names
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, descending through the maintenance door the keys open, into flooded Old Marlow — streetlights still burning underwater, a gymnasium with a scoreboard counting down. The chat's members appear, kids preserved by being remembered wrong. Lena, their captain, explains the rules of the memory championship. Beat: awe and grief entangled.

chapters.title: The Real Championship
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The contest: hold every true memory of Priya against the chat's versions, which are kinder, easier, and false. Round by round he loses pieces — her middle name, her brother's face — while Dez, topside, feeds him real memories through the buzzing phone. Beat: love as an act of stubborn accuracy.

chapters.title: Give Them Your Best One
chapters.summary: Climax. Noor's POV. To break Lena's hold, he must surrender his single most precious memory — his mother's face, the one thing keeping him afloat. He gives it up, names Priya truly one last time, and the flooded town lets them both go. Lena, finally remembered correctly by name, dissolves the chat. Beat: the price of survival paid in full.

chapters.title: One Unread Message
chapters.summary: Resolution. Noor's POV, three weeks later. Priya is back; nobody questions the missing days, and no one remembers Noor's win — or his mother. He carries a photo he can't feel anything toward, and Priya remembers for both of them. In his pocket, the brass keys. On a dead phone, the group chat flickers: one unread message. Beat: survival as a scar you learn to live beside.
